extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers submitting to / evaluating the NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks Track
extracted.subtask_short: NeurIPS 2024 D&B Track call for papers and review criteria
extracted.subtask_description: Official NeurIPS 2024 Datasets & Benchmarks Track Call for Papers. Lists scope, submission requirements, supplementary material requirements, and the explicit reviewing criteria the program committee will apply to dataset and benchmark submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility: dataset available without personal request, code open source
rubrics_metrics.description: A key criterion is accessibility: datasets should be available and accessible, i.e. the data can be found and obtained without a personal request to the PI, and any required code should be open source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as 'a key criterion'. We encourage the authors to use Croissant format (https://mlcommons.org/working-groups/data/croissant/) to document their datasets in machine readable way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Croissant machine-readable metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: URL to Croissant metadata record documenting the dataset/benchmark available for viewing and downloading by the reviewers. You can create your Croissant metadata using e.g. the Python library available here: https://github.com/mlcommons/croissant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in the supplementary materials for new-dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-credentialized access only when justified by public good
rubrics_metrics.description: This will be possible on the condition that a credentialization is necessary for the public good (e.g. because of ethically sensitive medical data), and that an established credentialization procedure is in place that is 1) open to a large section of the public, 2) provides rapid response and access to the data, and 3) is guaranteed to be maintained for many years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good example here is PhysioNet Credentialing... This should be seen as an exceptional measure, and NOT as a way to limit access to data for other reasons (e.g. to shield data behind a Data Transfer Agreement). Misuse would be grounds for desk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility, quality, impact, originality, novelty, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility and quality of the submission: Impact, originality, novelty, relevance to the NeurIPS community will all be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First listed criterion under 'All submissions' for the reviewing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility: sufficient information to reproduce results
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions should be accompanied by sufficient information to reproduce the results described i.e. all necessary datasets, code, and evaluation procedures must be accessible and documented. We encourage the use of a reproducibility framework such as the ML reproducibility checklist to guarantee that all results can be easily reproduced. Benchmark submissions in particular should take care to ensure sufficient details are provided to ensure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submissions include code, please refer to the NeurIPS code submission guidelines. Was code provided (e.g. in the supplementary material)? If provided, did you look at the code? Did you consider it useful in guiding your review? If not provided, did you wish code had been available?

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics: address ethical implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethics: Any ethical implications of the work should be addressed. Authors should rely on NeurIPS ethics guidelines as guidance for understanding ethical concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all submissions; in select cases where ethical concerns are flagged by reviewers, an ethics review may be performed as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of dataset documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, datasets must be accompanied by documentation communicating the details of the dataset as part of their submissions via structured templates (e.g. TODO). Sufficient detail must be provided on how the data was collected and organized, what kind of information it contains, ethically and responsibly, and how it will be made available and maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended documentation frameworks include datasheets for datasets, dataset nutrition labels, data statements for NLP, data cards, and accountability frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and access terms preventing misuse
rubrics_metrics.description: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, authors should provide licenses for any datasets released. These should consider the intended use and limitations of the dataset, and develop licenses and terms of use to prevent misuse or inappropriate use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit license required (ideally a CC license for datasets, or an open source license for code such as RL environments). An overview of licenses can be found at https://paperswithcode.com/datasets/license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Per NeurIPS ethics guidelines, datasets should minimize the exposure of any personally identifiable information, unless informed consent from those individuals is provided to do so. Any paper that chooses to create a dataset with real data of real people should ask for the explicit consent of participants, or explain why they were unable to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required for dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and responsible use, including for reused datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ethical implications of new datasets should be addressed and guidelines for responsible use should be provided where appropriate. Note that, if your submission includes publicly available datasets (e.g. as part of a larger benchmark), you should also check these datasets for ethical issues. You remain responsible for the ethical implications of including existing datasets or other data sources in your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibility extends to existing/third-party datasets included in benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal compliance with regional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal compliance: For datasets, authors should ensure awareness and compliance with regional legal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a dataset-specific evaluation factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosting, licensing, and maintenance plan. The choice of hosting platform is yours, as long as you ensure access to the data (possibly through a curated interface) and will provide the necessary maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in the supplementary materials for new-dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term preservation: It must be clear that the dataset will be available for a long time, either by uploading to a data repository or by explaining how the authors themselves will ensure this
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required item in dataset supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open and widely used data format with clear read instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset itself should ideally use an open and widely used data format. Provide a detailed explanation on how the dataset can be read. For simulation environments, use existing frameworks or explain how they can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required item in dataset supplementary materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured web-discoverable metadata (schema.org / DCAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add structured metadata to a dataset's meta-data page using Web standards (like schema.org and DCAT): This allows it to be discovered and organized by anyone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guide can be found here: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/data-types/dataset. If you use an existing data repository, this is often done automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent dereferenceable identifier (DOI / identifiers.org / code repo)
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly recommended: a persistent dereferenceable identifier (e.g. a DOI minted by a data repository or a prefix on identifiers.org) for datasets, or a code repository (e.g. GitHub, GitLab,...) for code. If this is not possible or useful, please explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highly recommended for the supplementary materials of dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility statement and license confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Author statement that they bear all responsibility in case of violation of rights, etc., and confirmation of the data license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required item in the supplementary materials for new-dataset submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure and description of LLM use in the paper
rubrics_metrics.description: we expect papers to fully describe their methodology, and any tool that is important to that methodology, including the use of LLMs, should be described also. For example, authors should mention tools (including LLMs) that were used for data processing or filtering, visualization, facilitating or running experiments, and proving theorems. It may also be advisable to describe the use of LLMs in implementing the method (if this corresponds to an important, original, or non-standard component of the approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are responsible for the entire content of the paper, including all text and figures, so while authors are welcome to use any tool they wish for writing the paper, they must ensure that all text is correct and original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer access to dataset during review
rubrics_metrics.description: The datasets themselves should be accessible to reviewers but can be publicly released at a later date (see below).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links to access the dataset and its metadata can be hidden upon submission if the dataset is not yet publicly available but must be added in the camera-ready version. In select cases, e.g when the data can only be released at a later date, this can be added afterward (up to a year after the submission deadline).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission discussion of prior reviewer concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: For papers resubmitted after being retracted from another venue: a brief discussion on the main concerns raised by previous reviewers and how you addressed them. You do not need to share the original reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required item in the supplementary materials for resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equally stringent review tailored to datasets/benchmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: We are aiming for an equally stringent review as the main conference, yet better suited to datasets and benchmarks. Submissions to this track will be reviewed according to a set of criteria and best practices specifically designed for datasets and benchmarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing statement at the start of the criteria section.
